title: Glaciers and the Rivers They Feed

endcard.line: Footage: NASA, Jesse Allen (public domain). Pictures: Arpit Rawat (CC0); Anshulsawant (public domain); NASA Earth Observatory (public domain)

segments.say: Thirty kilometres of ice. That is the length of the Gangotri glacier, one of the largest in the Himalayas.

anim.title: What a glacier is
items: Snow piles up year after year

segments.say: A glacier is a mass of ice moving slowly downhill because of gravity. It may move a few centimetres to a few metres a day.
As it moves, it scrapes its valley into a wide U shape, and leaves heaps of rock and debris behind.
At its snout, called Gaumukh, the ice melts. This is where the Bhagirathi, a headstream of the Ganga, is born.

right.title: Peninsular
items: many shrink in the dry season

segments.say: Because Himalayan rivers are fed by melting snow as well as rain, they flow all year. Geographers call them perennial.
But Gangotri has been shrinking since seventeen eighty. NASA found it retreated more than eight hundred and fifty metres in twenty-five years.
For GS One: glaciers are slow rivers of ice, and they keep the great Himalayan rivers flowing through the dry months.

sources: NASA Earth Observatory, 'Retreat of the Gangotri Glacier': 30.2 km long, 0.5–2.5 km wide, one of the largest in the Himalaya; receding since 1780, faster after 1971; retreated more than 850 m over the last 25 years (to 2001)

NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 3 (Drainage System): the Bhagirathi rises in the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh (3,900 m); Himalayan rivers are perennial because they are fed by melting snow and precipitation

NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 6 (Landforms and their Evolution): glaciers move because of gravity, a few centimetres to a few metres a day; glacial erosion and deposition landforms

quiz.q: Which river is born at Gaumukh, the snout of the Gangotri glacier?
quiz.why: The Bhagirathi rises at Gaumukh; the Alaknanda rises at Satopanth glacier.

quiz.q: Why do Himalayan rivers flow all year?
options: They are fed by both snow melt and rain
They are fed only by groundwater
They are dammed at the source
It rains every day in the Himalayas
quiz.why: Snow melt plus rain makes them perennial.

quiz.q: What shape of valley does a glacier carve?
quiz.why: Glacial erosion widens valleys into a U shape.

reviewNote: Facts were read against NASA Earth Observatory's Gangotri page and NCERT Class 11 (India: Physical Environment ch. 3; Fundamentals of Physical Geography ch. 6). The U-shaped valley is standard NCERT glacial-landform content; confirm the wording in ch. 6 if needed. The NASA retreat image shows terminus lines but no borders. Moving facts: Gangotri's length and retreat figures are from NASA's 2001-era analysis; newer studies give other numbers.
